new_episodes.source_paraphrase: On 3 September, Mathspace took Metabase offline, revoked its API keys, disabled its Australian and US Snowflake access accounts, changed database passwords and preserved investigation copies.
new_episodes.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Containment and evidence preservation do not demonstrate completed system recovery.

new_episodes.source_paraphrase: School contacts and regulators were notified on 4 September. Individual notifications began on 6 September, earlier than the schedule initially given to schools.
new_episodes.recovered_invariant_interpretation: School coordination, regulator reporting and individual notices have different recipients and dates.

new_episodes.source_paraphrase: The 8 September update reported 1,079,819 affected people and clarified account metadata omitted from earlier communications. Academic records and authentication credentials were excluded. It reported no evidence of later misuse; individual notices and recovery checks remained ongoing.
new_episodes.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Corrected disclosure scope and unfinished response work remain material.

explicit_evidence_changes.old_value: Mathspace disclosed that attackers exploited a vulnerability in its self-hosted Metabase reporting system, obtained administrator access without a legitimate login, and downloaded personal information from its Australian reporting database. Mathspace identified 1,079,819 affected people across Australia and New Zealand, including students, parents or guardians, teachers and Mathspace staff. Exposed fields included names, usernames, email addresses and account metadata. Mathspace states that academic records, assessment results, passwords, authentication tokens, SSO credentials and API credentials were not exposed.
explicit_evidence_changes.new_value: Mathspace disclosed that attackers exploited a vulnerability in its self-hosted Metabase reporting system, obtained administrator access without a legitimate login, and downloaded personal information from its Australian reporting database. Mathspace identified 1,079,819 affected people across Australia and New Zealand, including students, parents or guardians, teachers and Mathspace staff. Exposed fields included names, usernames, email addresses and account metadata. Mathspace states that academic records, assessment results, passwords, authentication tokens, SSO credentials and API credentials were not exposed. After reviewing logs, Mathspace confirmed the breach on 3 September and disabled the affected reporting access. It notified schools and regulators on 4 September and began individual notices on 6 September. Its 8 September update clarified that earlier communications had omitted some exposed account details; recovery checks and notifications were still continuing.
explicit_evidence_changes.reason: Merged duplicate log/reconstruction clauses and restored access, download, patch-before-discovery, containment, notification and corrected disclosure stages.
